# Crème Brûlée

From the notebook behind the bar at the bistro on Rue Saint-A. The chef there wrote this out for me on a napkin and I've been making it the same way for a decade.

Serves 6

Ingredients:
- 1 quart heavy cream
- 1 vanilla bean, split, seeds scraped (or 2 tsp vanilla extract)
- 6 egg yolks
- 3/4 cup sugar, plus more for the tops
- pinch of salt

Method:
Preheat the oven to 325F. Combine cream, vanilla bean and seeds in a saucepan and bring just to a simmer, then take it off the heat and let it steep briefly, off the heat, until fragrant.

Whisk the yolks with the sugar and salt until pale. Slowly stream in the warm cream, whisking the whole time so the eggs don't scramble. Strain through a fine sieve into a jug.

Divide among six ramekins set in a deep roasting pan. Fill the pan with hot water halfway up the sides of the ramekins.

Cook time: 40 minutes in the water bath, until the custards are set at the edges but still wobble in the center like set jelly.

Lift the ramekins out, cool to room temperature, then chill overnight, uncovered, in the fridge.

Just before serving, sprinkle a thin even layer of sugar on top of each and torch it until it's dark amber and cracks like glass under a spoon.
